context_profiles.regimen_role: Weekly cetuximab + head and neck radiotherapy
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Cetuximab is combined with radiotherapy for selected locally advanced head and neck cancer when platinum chemotherapy is unsuitable. The team discusses the reason for choosing this treatment and the alternatives.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced squamous head and neck cancer in people ineligible for platinum-based treatment.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab binds to EGFR, a receptor involved in growth and repair. It helps radiotherapy work against selected head and neck cancers. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, which helps explain acne-like rash, dryness and nail changes. Radiotherapy directs radiation at a carefully planned area. It is delivered on its own appointment calendar. Effects depend on which tissues receive radiation and can build up during the course or continue after it finishes.
context_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab starts one week before radiotherapy: a 400 mg/m² first infusion, then 250 mg/m² every week during radiation until radiotherapy ends. The number of weekly doses follows the actual radiotherapy plan.
key_points: Locally advanced squamous head and neck cancer in people ineligible for platinum-based treatment.

Cetuximab starts one week before radiotherapy: a 400 mg/m² first infusion, then 250 mg/m² every week during radiation until radiotherapy ends. The number of weekly doses follows the actual radiotherapy plan.

Blood count, kidney and liver function with electrolytes, magnesium and calcium. Review allergies, previous reactions, red-meat allergy or tick bites. Before head and neck radiation, arrange dental, nutrition and swallowing assessment with the team.

Blood count, kidney/liver function and minerals are reviewed regularly as specified in the treatment plan. Vitals and symptoms are checked around infusions; skin, eyes, breathing and hydration are reviewed. Radiation has its own weekly support and assessment plan.

Electrolytes, magnesium and calcium monthly for two months after the final cetuximab dose. Continue skin, dental, nutrition, swallowing and radiation follow-up. Scans and examinations follow the individual cancer plan; no universal scan date or tumour-marker test is required by this regimen.
No RAS requirement is imported from colorectal cetuximab. Resolve NCCP versus product-information observation requirements explicitly.

shared_decision_focus: Discuss the individual aim, alternatives and uncertainty; serious or lasting harms; treatment burden; fertility and pregnancy precautions; and the patient’s priorities. Explain infusion anaphylaxis, rash and nail/eye problems, mineral loss and post-treatment testing; the observation plan requires reconciliation of NCCP and product information. supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Minimal for cetuximab; radiotherapy support separately required
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Cetuximab before radiotherapy: Antihistamine and corticosteroid premedication — Before the first cetuximab infusion; strongly recommended for subsequent infusions Individual clinician/pharmacy prescription required.

patient_education: Tell staff immediately about an infusion reaction. After leaving, seek urgent help for swelling, wheeze, faintness or breathing difficulty. Report spreading rash, infected nails, eye pain, visual change, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink. Mouth and skin effects from radiation may continue after its final session.
special_support: Ask for one schedule showing prevention medicines, rescue treatment and what to do if symptoms persist. Do not add, double or restart medicines from an old prescription.

Premedication helps reduce infusion reactions; the team also provides a skin-care plan. Keep mineral blood-test appointments, including monthly checks for two months after the final dose. Report delayed reactions even after earlier infusions were tolerated.

A dietitian can tailor food texture, supplements and calorie or protein needs. Tell the team early if eating or drinking becomes difficult; do not wait for substantial weight loss. Fluid targets depend on kidney and heart health.

Use the mouth-care plan provided by the team and tell them about ulcers, thrush, bleeding or pain. Inform your dentist about cancer treatment. Before any dental procedure, confirm timing with the oncology team.

A speech and language therapist can assess swallowing and advise exercises or safer food and drink textures. Follow the individual assessment; a general guide cannot decide which textures are safe for you.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before treatment and the medicine-specific duration of contraception afterwards. Ask about breastfeeding. Bring a full medicine, supplement and allergy list; check before adding over-the-counter or herbal products.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: The aim is to control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. The team reviews how well treatment is working and whether side effects remain acceptable; there is no single fixed number of cycles for everyone.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Irinotecan: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1 FOLFIRI includes irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat the reference cycle every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.
route_and_duration: Fortnightly cetuximab infusion time is set from the dose and safe infusion rate; the first dose may take longer. regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Shared PD-1 monotherapy protocol. Select the exact NCCP indication and treatment setting; dedicated services below distinguish lung, colorectal where available, and the authored melanoma pathways.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks (21 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.
key_points: Minimal emetic risk; no usual routine premedication.
No pembrolizumab dose reduction; apply specific hold/permanent-stop and restart criteria.
Grade 4/recurrent grade3 generic immune rules have specific endocrine exceptions; controlled hypothyroidism need not interrupt treatment.
Creatinine is ×ULN, never ×baseline; hepatitis and nephritis thresholds must not be confused with stable organ impairment recommendations.
Every-3–6-week thyroid checks continue on both infusion schedules.
Shared clinical protocol; new patient suite is lung-only.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

Requested restart needs documented source-specific recovery, required steroid management/taper and consultant confirmation. Table 1 endocrine exceptions remain separate; existing 12-week failure/taper and permanent-stop criteria retain priority.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

Shared-protocol eligibility audit now includes head-and-neck, adjuvant RCC, urothelial and cervical maintenance selection. These are distinct from the existing lung, colorectal and melanoma patient-service contexts.

treatment_rationale.summary: PD-1 blockade restores antitumour T-cell activity. First-line metastatic and post-resection adjuvant NSCLC have separate populations, treatment goals and evidence; the shared protocol does not make their eligibility interchangeable.
treatment_rationale.setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
treatment_rationale.line: First-line metastatic OR post-resection adjuvant after platinum chemotherapy
factors: Confirm the exact lung indication and treatment aim. Metastatic first-line: validated PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, no EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, stage IV, no prior systemic metastatic treatment, ECOG 0–1.

Adjuvant: complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy, high recurrence-risk/pathological stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 source criteria, ECOG 0–1; confirm reimbursement/access separately. No metastatic TPS50 eligibility requirement applies.

FBC, renal and liver profiles, glucose and thyroid function. Review autoimmune disease, prior interstitial lung disease, infection, untreated brain metastases, steroid/immunosuppressive use, prior checkpoint treatment, pregnancy/breastfeeding and medicines.
alternatives: Choose among available systemic, targeted, clinical-trial, surveillance and supportive-care options using the precise setting, biomarkers, comorbidity and patient preferences.
limitations: These lung trials used pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks. Trial treatment limits and research scan schedules are not automatic NCCP prescribing rules.

KEYNOTE-024: selected untreated metastatic TPS≥50%, no sensitising EGFR/ALK; 66% effective crossover to subsequent PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in the chemotherapy group. Results are not for the adjuvant setting.

KEYNOTE-091 final analysis was presented at ESMO 2026 and reported by the trial sponsor EORTC on 27 October 2026. Chemotherapy-subgroup DFS remained improved; overall survival was not significantly improved at this final, time-triggered analysis. This is conference/sponsor reporting rather than a new full peer-reviewed article. Do not mix these figures with earlier EMA interim snapshots or the trial-wide population.
NCCP adjuvant NSCLC access is listed N/A; verify reimbursement. Trial schedules, efficacy and licensing are not identical to funded access.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 400 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 6 weeks (42 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.

endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to death from any cause.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

context_profiles.component_rationale: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that make it harder for cells to repair and divide. During chemoradiation it also increases the effect of radiotherapy. regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab and chemotherapy aim to control head and neck cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be removed. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for you.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in adults with tumour PD-L1 CPS ≥1.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can limit the activity of immune cells. This can help them attack cancer, but can also cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it ends. Carboplatin interferes with DNA repair and cell division. Its dose is calculated from kidney function. Blood counts can fall, including platelets that help stop bleeding. It is a different prescription from cisplatin. Fluorouracil interferes with the materials cells need to make DNA and RNA. A pump gives it over the prescribed days. DPD is an enzyme that helps break it down; testing before treatment reduces risk but cannot prevent every severe reaction.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab and carboplatin on Day 1; fluorouracil over Days 1–4. Up to 6 combination cycles, then pembrolizumab alone while appropriate. Every dose depends on safety and benefit review.
key_points: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in adults with tumour PD-L1 CPS ≥1.

Every 21 days: pembrolizumab and carboplatin on Day 1; fluorouracil over Days 1–4. Up to 6 combination cycles, then pembrolizumab alone while appropriate. Every dose depends on safety and benefit review.

Blood count, kidney and liver function, glucose and thyroid tests; hepatitis B surface antigen/core antibody and hepatitis C; tumour PD-L1 CPS and DPD assessment before fluorouracil. Review previous immune problems, transplants, medicines and infection. An isotope GFR measurement is preferred when assessing kidney function for carboplatin dosing; further kidney testing is arranged when indicated. Audiology is considered when indicated.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose each cycle; thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks and sooner if symptoms require. Ask about bowel, breathing, skin, hormone and other immune symptoms before every dose. A normal blood test does not exclude immune toxicity.

Continue reporting possible immune effects after the last dose. Follow unresolved blood, kidney, hearing, nerve or endocrine problems and any prescribed steroid taper or hormone replacement. The team sets disease assessment scans and follow-up; this protocol does not mandate a universal imaging interval or routine blood tumour-marker schedule.
PD-L1 uses CPS ≥1, not the lung-cancer TPS threshold. DPD assessment and fluorouracil contraindications must be checked.
Use up to six combination cycles followed by pembrolizumab maintenance; no automatic 24-month cap is inserted.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can limit the activity of immune cells. This can help them attack cancer, but can also cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it ends. Cisplatin forms links in DNA that make it harder for cells to repair and divide. In this regimen it is combined with fluorouracil and pembrolizumab to treat cancer throughout the body. Healthy cells can be affected, which is why kidney, blood, hearing and nerve checks matter. Fluorouracil interferes with the materials cells need to make DNA and RNA. A pump gives it over the prescribed days. DPD is an enzyme that helps break it down; testing before treatment reduces risk but cannot prevent every severe reaction.
